recipes.name: Lentil & Chard Soup
recipes.health: About 14 g plant protein, 10 g fibre and 5 mg iron per bowl. The lemon helps your body absorb the iron. Recipe after Lentil Soup with Swiss Chard (Adass bel-Hamud) in The Taste of Beirut, with less oil in the pesto. Source: AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines, guideline 6. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 bunch Swiss chard (about 300 g, or spinach), chopped
Cilantro pesto: 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 bunch cilantro leaves (about 30 g), 8 garlic cloves pounded to a paste with 1 tsp salt
Juice of 2 lemons, plus 1 lemon cut in quarters to serve
recipes.method:
1. Heat the 3 tbsp olive oil in a soup pot and cook the onion until golden, about 8 minutes.
2. Add the rinsed lentils and the water. Simmer 45 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
3. Add the chard and simmer 10 minutes more.
4. Make the pesto: heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan for 1 minute, add the chopped cilantro and the garlic paste and stir for a few seconds until it smells strong. Stir it into the soup for the last 3 minutes.
5. Add the lemon juice, taste, and serve warm with the lemon quarters to squeeze in.

recipes.name: Green Protein Smoothie
recipes.health: About 20 g protein, 6 g fibre, and more than a full day of vitamin K from the spinach. Greek yoghurt gives the protein, flax adds fibre and plant omega-3. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Wash the spinach. Put the water, yoghurt and spinach in the blender first, then the banana, flaxseed and ice.
2. Blend for 1 minute, until completely smooth.
3. Drink at once, or within 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Chia & Walnuts
recipes.health: About 31 g protein and 13 g fibre. Oat beta-glucan (about 2 g here) is the fibre that lowers LDL cholesterol; the US FDA accepts this claim at 3 g a day. Soak-in-the-fridge method as in the Peach Muesli of 365 Days of Healthy Eating. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. In a jar, mix the oats, chia, milk, yoghurt and cinnamon.
2. Close the jar and leave it in the fridge overnight, at least 6 hours.
3. In the morning, stir. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
4. Top with the blueberries and walnuts. Eat cold.
5. Keep it cold. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Chicken & Quinoa Bowl
recipes.health: About 55 g protein and 6 g fibre per bowl, for muscle repair after training. Quinoa gives slow carbs and fibre; olive oil and lemon make the dressing. Source: AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Rinse the quinoa. Boil it in 250 ml water for 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Cover and rest 5 minutes.
2. Cut each chicken breast in half through the thickness so it cooks evenly. Rub with half the oil, the cumin and half the salt.
3. Cook in a hot pan, about 5 minutes each side, until the middle reaches 74°C and no pink is left. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
4. Mix the lemon juice, garlic, the rest of the oil and salt for the dressing.
5. Put quinoa, spinach, cucumber and tomatoes in two bowls. Add the chicken and pour the dressing on top.
6. Wash your hands, knife and board after touching the raw chicken. Keep leftovers in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.name: Baked Salmon with Lemon & Broccoli
recipes.health: About 34 g protein and 3 g omega-3 (EPA and DHA) per serving. The American Heart Association advises fish twice a week for a healthy heart. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 lemon (juice of half, the rest in slices)
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 200°C.
2. Put the broccoli on a tray with half the oil, the garlic and a pinch of salt. Bake 10 minutes.
3. Push the broccoli aside. Add the salmon, skin down. Season with salt, pepper, the rest of the oil and the lemon juice. Lay the lemon slices on top.
4. Bake 12 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and the middle reaches 63°C. Serve at once.
5. Keep leftovers in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.name: Heart Nut & Seed Mix
recipes.health: A 36 g handful gives about 7 g protein and 3 g fibre. The US FDA allows the claim that 1.5 oz (42 g) of nuts a day, in a low-saturated-fat diet, may reduce heart disease risk. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Mix everything in a jar. No salt, no sugar.
2. Keep it closed in a cool, dry place.
3. One handful (about 36 g) a day. The jar lasts a week.

recipes.name: Blueberry Oat Shake
recipes.health: About 25 g protein and 8 g fibre. Oats bring beta-glucan, the fibre the US FDA links to lower cholesterol (3 g a day); this glass gives about half of that. Blueberries add vitamin C. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put the milk, yoghurt and oats in the blender and leave 5 minutes so the oats soften.
2. Add the blueberries and cinnamon.
3. Blend for 1 minute, until smooth. Drink at once.

recipes.name: Foul Moudammas
recipes.health: About 20 g plant protein and 17 g fibre per serving, with iron and folate. Fava beans are a staple legume in the AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines for Lebanon. Their fibre slows the rise in blood sugar. Recipe after Fava Bean Soup (Ful Mudammas) in The Taste of Beirut, with much less oil. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 400 g cooked fava beans (one tin, drained)
2 garlic cloves, pounded to a paste with the salt
recipes.method:
1. Drain the fava beans and put them in a pan with the fresh water. Cook 15 minutes on low to medium heat.
2. Mash about one third of the beans with a fork and cook a few minutes more, until it is very thick.
3. Stir in the garlic paste, lemon juice, olive oil and parsley. Taste and adjust.
4. Serve in a bowl topped with the diced tomato.

recipes.name: Chickpea Tabbouleh
recipes.health: About 17 g plant protein and 14 g fibre per serving. Parsley is very rich in vitamin K and vitamin C, chickpeas add protein and slow-release carbs, olive oil gives the heart-friendly fats. Recipe after Classic Tabbouleh in The Taste of Beirut; we add chickpeas for protein. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central; legumes as in the AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines.
ingredients: 2 big bunches fresh parsley (about 120 g leaves)
1 small bunch fresh mint (20 g leaves)
recipes.method:
1. Wash and dry the parsley, mint, tomatoes and spring onions well. Pick the leaves and chop the parsley and mint very fine.
2. Dice the tomatoes and keep their juice. Soak the bulgur in the tomato juice for 20 minutes, then drain and squeeze it.
3. Mix the parsley, mint, tomatoes, spring onions, bulgur and chickpeas in a large bowl.
4. Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, salt and allspice. Pour over just before serving so the herbs stay fresh, and toss.
5. Keep in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.name: Hummus with Veggie Sticks
recipes.health: About 8 g plant protein and 7 g fibre per serving. Chickpeas and sesame (tahini) give protein, fibre and unsaturated fats, and the raw vegetables add crunch for almost no calories. Recipe after Classic Hummus (Hummus M'tabbal) in The Taste of Beirut. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 garlic clove, pounded to a paste with the salt
recipes.method:
1. Keep 2 tbsp of the chickpeas aside for the garnish. Stir the tahini well in its jar.
2. Blend the rest of the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic paste and water until completely smooth. If it is too thick add a little water from the tin.
3. Spoon into a bowl, pour the olive oil in a ring on top, sprinkle the paprika and add the whole chickpeas.
4. Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks. Keep in the fridge and eat within 4 days.

recipes.name: Fish & Chickpea Tomato Bake
recipes.health: About 45 g protein and 12 g fibre per serving. White fish is lean protein and a source of vitamin B12 and selenium; the American Heart Association recommends fish at least twice a week. Chickpeas and tomatoes add fibre and lycopene. Beirut-style flavours (cumin, garlic, cilantro, lemon) from Spiced Fish in The Taste of Beirut, baked instead of fried. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 2 white fish fillets, 150 g each (cod or sea bream)
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 200°C.
2. In a baking dish mix the onion, garlic, tomatoes, chickpeas, cumin, chilli, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
3. Bake 15 minutes.
4. Lay the fish on top, drizzle with the rest of the olive oil and bake 12–15 minutes more, until it flakes easily and the middle reaches 63°C.
5. Scatter with cilantro and serve with the lemon wedges.
6. Keep leftovers in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.name: Strawberry Yoghurt Shake
recipes.health: About 25 g protein and close to a full day of vitamin C from the strawberries. Almonds add vitamin E and unsaturated fats. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put the milk, yoghurt and almonds in the blender and blend 30 seconds.
2. Add the strawberries and ice.
3. Blend 1 minute, until smooth. Drink at once.

recipes.name: Cucumber Mint Ayran
recipes.health: About 20 g protein for only 135 kcal, plus calcium. A traditional Lebanese yoghurt drink: light, cooling, no sugar. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put the yoghurt, water, cucumber, mint and salt in the blender.
2. Blend 30 seconds, until smooth.
3. Pour over the ice and drink cold.

recipes.name: Spinach & Tomato Omelette
recipes.health: About 15 g protein. Eggs give vitamin B12, vitamin D and choline; spinach adds folate and vitamin K. Cooked with a little olive oil, not butter. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan on medium heat. Add the spinach and tomato and cook 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
2. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them over the vegetables.
3. Cook 2 to 3 minutes without stirring, until no liquid egg is left. Fold in half and serve.

recipes.name: Warm Oat Porridge with Apple & Walnuts
recipes.health: About 18 g protein and 9 g fibre. Oats bring beta-glucan: the US FDA links 3 g a day to lower cholesterol, and this bowl gives about two thirds of that. Walnuts add plant omega-3. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put the oats and milk in a small pot and cook on medium heat 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
2. Stir in the apple and cinnamon and cook 1 more minute.
3. Pour into a bowl and top with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Tuna & White Bean Salad
recipes.health: About 28 g protein and 11 g fibre per serving. Tuna is rich in vitamin B12 and selenium, and the American Heart Association recommends fish twice a week. White beans add slow-release carbs. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 160 g canned tuna in water, drained (about 2 small tins)
240 g cooked white beans (one tin, drained)
1/2 small red onion (50 g), thinly sliced
recipes.method:
1. Put the beans, tomatoes, onion and parsley in a bowl.
2. Flake the tuna over the top.
3. Dress with the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Toss gently and serve.
4. Keep in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.name: Mujaddara with Cucumber Yoghurt
recipes.health: About 15 g protein and 13 g fibre per serving. Lentils plus a grain make a complete plant protein; legumes are a staple in the AUB Food-Based Dietary Guidelines for Lebanon. Recipe after Mujaddara Hamra in The Taste of Beirut, with the onions browned in a little oil instead of deep-fried. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 100 g dry green or brown lentils
2 large onions (300 g): 1 chopped fine, 1 sliced in rings
Salad: 200 g cucumber, diced | 150 g plain Greek yoghurt, 0% fat
recipes.method:
1. Simmer the lentils in 500 ml water for 20 minutes.
2. Cook the chopped onion in 1 tbsp of the olive oil until golden brown and add it to the lentils.
3. Add the bulgur and cook about 20 minutes, until the lentils and bulgur are soft and the water is gone. Add the cumin and salt 10 minutes before the end. If it is still hard, add a splash of water.
4. Cook the onion rings in the other tbsp of oil on medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
5. Mix the cucumber into the yoghurt.
6. Top the lentils with the onion rings and serve with the cucumber yoghurt and radishes.

recipes.name: Roasted Spiced Chickpeas
recipes.health: About 7 g plant protein and 6 g fibre per serving: a crunchy snack with no added sugar. Low and slow method as in Cooking Light Annual Recipes 2013 (Crunchy Chickpeas). Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 150°C.
2. Wrap the chickpeas in a clean towel and roll them lightly to loosen the skins. Pick out and throw away the skins.
3. Mix the chickpeas with the olive oil, cumin, paprika, garlic and salt and spread on a baking tray.
4. Bake 1 hour 40 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes, until dry and crunchy.
5. Let them cool on the tray. Eat the same day: in a closed jar they go soft.

recipes.name: Yoghurt, Walnut & Pomegranate Cup
recipes.health: About 22 g protein. Walnuts carry a US FDA qualified health claim for heart health (about 43 g a day; this cup has about half), and pomegranate adds vitamin C. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 60 g pomegranate seeds (about 1/3 of a pomegranate)
recipes.method:
1. Spoon the yoghurt into a glass or bowl.
2. Top with the walnuts and pomegranate seeds.
3. Sprinkle with the cinnamon.

recipes.name: Lemon Garlic Chicken with Roasted Zucchini
recipes.health: About 45 g protein per serving for 405 kcal. Chicken breast is a lean protein; zucchini adds vitamin C and potassium for very few calories. Sauce and method after Lemon Chicken (Djaj be Hamoud) in Everyday Lebanese Cooking (Hamadeh), with chicken breast and zucchini instead of a whole chicken and potatoes. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 400 g chicken breast, cut in 4 pieces
400 g zucchini, cut in thick half-moons
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 200°C.
2. Brush the chicken with 1/2 tbsp of the oil in one bowl and toss the zucchini with 1/2 tbsp in another, so the raw chicken never touches the vegetables. Spread both on a baking tray and bake 15 minutes.
3. Meanwhile mix the coriander, garlic, lemon juice, the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the salt and pepper.
4. Spoon the sauce over the chicken and zucchini, cover the tray with foil and bake 15 minutes more, until the thickest piece reaches 74°C and no pink is left.
5. Serve hot.
6. Wash your hands, knife and board after touching the raw chicken. Keep leftovers in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.name: Baked Musaqa'a
recipes.health: About 7 g plant protein and 13 g fibre per serving. A Lebanese eggplant, tomato and chickpea stew, baked instead of fried. Tomatoes add lycopene. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 2 medium eggplants (500 g), cut in thick rounds
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 220°C. Brush the eggplant rounds with 1 tbsp of the olive oil and bake on a tray 20 minutes, until soft and golden.
2. Meanwhile cook the onion and garlic in the other tbsp of oil for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, cumin and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
3. Stir the chickpeas into the sauce.
4. In a baking dish layer the eggplant and the sauce. Bake 15 minutes and serve.

recipes.name: Banana Oat Peanut Shake
recipes.health: About 19 g protein and 5 g fibre. Oats bring beta-glucan, the fibre the US FDA links to lower cholesterol. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 tbsp natural peanut butter (no added sugar)
recipes.method:
1. Put everything in a blender.
2. Blend 45 seconds until smooth.
3. Drink at once.

recipes.name: Cocoa Banana Yoghurt Shake
recipes.health: About 23 g protein from yoghurt and milk. Ground flaxseed adds omega-3 (ALA) and fibre. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Put everything in a blender.
2. Blend 45 seconds until smooth.
3. Drink at once.

recipes.name: Tomato Pepper Shakshuka
recipes.health: About 12 g protein per serving from the eggs, with lycopene from cooked tomatoes and vitamin C from the pepper. Method after Eggs Poached in Tomato Stew in The Taste of Beirut (we add a red pepper). Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, pounded to a paste with the salt
recipes.method:
1. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan. Cook the onion and pepper about 15 minutes, until soft and golden.
2. Add the tomatoes with their juice and heat gently 10 minutes.
3. Stir in the garlic paste and heat 5 minutes more.
4. Make four small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
5. Cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes, until the whites are completely set (no clear egg left). Cook 2 minutes longer for a firm yolk. Serve from the pan.

recipes.name: Banana Oat Pancakes
recipes.health: No flour and no added sugar. The oats give beta-glucan fibre (US FDA heart-health claim) and the eggs add about 10 g protein per serving. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 tsp olive oil, for the pan
recipes.method:
1. Blend the bananas, oats, eggs and cinnamon into a thick batter. Rest 5 minutes.
2. Heat a non-stick pan with a little of the oil on medium heat.
3. Pour small rounds, about 3 tbsp each. Cook 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
4. Serve warm.
5. Do not taste the raw batter, it has raw egg. Cook every pancake until firm in the middle.

recipes.name: Lentil Spinach Feta Salad
recipes.health: About 20 g protein and 12 g fibre per serving. Lentils and spinach bring iron and folate; olive oil is the AUB Mediterranean-pattern fat. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Wash the spinach and tomatoes. Mix the olive oil, lemon juice and salt in a large bowl.
2. Add the lentils, spinach and tomatoes and toss.
3. Top with the feta and serve.
4. Keep cooked lentils in the fridge and use within 3 days.

recipes.name: Chicken Hummus Wrap
recipes.health: About 41 g protein per serving. Whole-wheat bread and hummus add fibre; chickpeas and sesame in the hummus give plant protein. Marinade after Grilled Chicken Sandwich (Sheesh Tawook) in The Taste of Beirut, with hummus in place of garlic cream. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 250 g chicken breast, cut in chunks (about 200 g cooked)
Marinade: 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp olive oil, 1 garlic clove pounded to a paste with a pinch of salt, 1/2 tsp paprika, 1/4 tsp salt, black pepper
recipes.method:
1. Mix the chicken with the marinade. Cover and keep in the fridge at least 30 minutes (overnight is even better).
2. Cook the chicken in a hot pan or on the grill, 5 to 6 minutes on each side, until the middle reaches 74°C and no pink is left. Let it cool a few minutes.
3. Spread the hummus over the two flatbreads and add the chicken, cucumber, tomato and lettuce. Roll tight and cut in half.
4. Wash your hands, knife and board after touching the raw chicken. Eat the wrap within a few hours or keep it chilled. Cooked chicken keeps 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Carrot Sticks with Tahini Dip
recipes.health: Carrots are rich in beta-carotene (vitamin A) and tahini adds calcium and sesame protein. A crunchy snack with no added sugar. Tahini and lemon in the proportion of the citrus-tahini sauce in The Taste of Beirut. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
recipes.method:
1. Wash and peel the carrots. Stir the tahini, lemon juice, water, garlic and salt until smooth and pourable.
2. Serve the carrot sticks with the dip.

recipes.name: Apple with Almond Butter
recipes.health: About 4 g fibre from the apple and healthy fats from the almonds. A slow-release snack that keeps blood sugar steadier than a sweet. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 1 tbsp natural almond butter (no added sugar)
recipes.method:
1. Wash the apple. Slice the apple into wedges.
2. Spread or dip with the almond butter and sprinkle the cinnamon.

recipes.name: Chicken Kafta Tray Bake
recipes.health: About 25 g lean protein per serving. Ground chicken keeps saturated fat low; parsley and the vegetables add vitamin K and C. Kafta paste and spices as in The Taste of Beirut (Accad), made with chicken instead of beef. Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 20 g flat parsley (a small bunch), roughly chopped
1/2 tsp paprika or mild Aleppo pepper
recipes.method:
1. Heat the oven to 220°C.
2. Pulse the onion in a food processor until very fine. Add the parsley, chicken, salt, allspice, cinnamon and paprika and process to a smooth paste.
3. Chill the paste 20 minutes, then shape into 9 finger-shaped kaftas.
4. Toss the zucchini and tomatoes with the olive oil on a large tray and add the kaftas.
5. Bake 20 to 25 minutes, turning the kaftas once, until golden and the middle of a kafta reaches 74°C, with no pink left.
6. Wash your hands, bowl and board after touching the raw chicken. Keep leftovers in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.name: Spinach Chickpea Stew
recipes.health: About 11 g plant protein and 10 g fibre per serving. Chickpeas and spinach bring iron, folate and magnesium. Garlic and coriander paste as in Spinach Stew in Lebanese Home Cooking (Mouzawak). Nutrition: USDA FoodData Central.
ingredients: 30 g fresh coriander (1 small bunch), chopped
recipes.method:
1. Cook the onion in the olive oil about 5 minutes, until soft and translucent.
2. Add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
3. Add the chickpeas, then the spinach in handfuls. It melts in a few minutes in its own water. Cook until the stew is as thick as you like.
4. Pound the garlic with the salt, add the coriander and pound to a coarse paste. Stir it into the stew, taste and serve hot.
